text:
maria (platform): Proposal: combine burst shaping (token-bucket + percentile-based refill) with per-org concurrency caps. want feedback on rules and console UI.

jon (infra): sounds good. do we enforce at edge LB or at router/serving layer?

alex (runtime): Prefer router-level admission + serving per-worker concurrency enforcement. router drops/queues based on effective credits.

sasha (prod-eng): need graceful degradation for committed customers — can we let Dedicated orgs exceed burst by consuming reserved credits?

maria (platform): yes — idea: three-tier credits: base_rate (rpm/tpm), burst_credits (refill per window based on historical p95), and reserved_commit credits for reserved capacity.

jon (infra): how to compute refill dynamically?

alex (runtime): algorithm idea:

```
# per-org config
rpm: 1200
tpm: 72000
concurrency: 12
burst_window_sec: 60
burst_credits: 300
refill_rate = percentile(usage_last_7d, 95) / burst_window_sec
```

alex (runtime): router tracks token-bucket and active_conns. if active_conns >= concurrency -> queue up to queue_limit else allow. tokens consumed per request = ceil(tokens_per_prompt)

sasha (prod-eng): queueing is fine but UX needs a clear signal in the console and telemetry. we should expose "burst_balance", "effective_concurrency", and "queue_time_ms" on per-org dashboard.

maria (platform): console mock: show a small gauge for Burst (0-100%), a numeric Effective Concurrency, and a timeline of burst credit refills.

jon (infra): telemetry: tag metrics with enforcement_point={edge,router,worker} and credit_type={base,burst,reserved}. alert on sustained queue_time_ms > 500ms across org_p90.

alex (runtime): fallback policy: when tokens depleted, but there is compatible model variant (quantized or smaller) we should auto-route low-priority requests to cheaper variant instead of outright 429.

sasha (prod-eng): edge cases: rapid spikes from small orgs that try to game bursts. propose a short cooldown per org when their refill rate jumps > 3x within 5m.

maria (platform): agree. also add telemetry for "burst_abuse_count" and automated soft-throttle if abuse detected.

jon (infra): ops question: how do billing and enforcement line up? we need to ensure billing derives from same accounting stream as credits refills to avoid mismatch.

maria (platform): same pipeline. we'll expose reconciliation metrics: billed_tokens vs accounted_tokens. set alert when diff > 0.5% in 1h.

alex (runtime): coding effort estimate: router + serving hooks ~ 3w, console + metrics ~ 2w, rollout: canary by org-size buckets.

sasha (prod-eng): rollout plan: 1) opt-in beta 2) gradual 10% usage 3) open to all with a 72h monitoring window and rollback if p99 latency regresses > 15%

maria (platform): next steps: write RFC with the algorithm above + console mocks. volunteers?

jon (infra): i'll take router enforcement design.

alex (runtime): i'll prototype token accounting in the runtime.

sasha (prod-eng): i'll own console mocks and telemetry mapping.

deploy-bot: scheduled deploy to staging at 2024-11-12T02:00Z :rocket:

maria (platform): thanks all. will draft RFC and ping for review by EOW :+1:
